title: On Reliability of Membership Inference Vulnerability Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2605.25819v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) are popular methods for empirically assessing the leakage of sensitive information in the training data through models or statistics learned from the data. The MI vulnerability is often evaluated through a binary classifier that tries to predict whether a particular sample was in the training data. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of MIAs multiple \textit{shadow models} are trained using random partitions of a larger dataset. After training the shadow models the MI vulnerability can be evaluated for all the samples for which we obtained shadow models. In order to evaluate the MI vulnerability reliably one needs a lot of shadow models which can be computationally infeasible. Therefore instead of reporting the actual sample level vulnerabilities aggregates over multiple samples are often reported in practice. translated_title: 关于成员推断漏洞评估可靠性的研究
translated_abstract: 成员推断攻击（MIA）是通过模型或从数据中学习到的统计信息来实证评估训练数据中敏感信息泄露的常用方法。成员推断（MI）漏洞通常通过一个二分类器来评估，该分类器试图预测某个特定样本是否存在于训练数据中。为了评估MIA的有效性，需要使用从更大数据集的随机划分中训练出的多个“影子模型”。在训练完影子模型后，可以对所有已获得影子模型的样本评估其成员推断漏洞。然而，为了可靠地评估成员推断漏洞，需要大量的影子模型，这在计算上可能是不可行的。因此，实践中通常不报告实际的样本级漏洞，而是报告多个样本的聚合结果。我们展示了典型MIA评估流程中的两个关键弱点。首先，我们展示了……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了典型的成员推断攻击评估流程中存在的两个关键弱点，指出由于训练大量影子模型在计算上不可行，实践中报告的聚合漏洞指标可能无法可靠地反映真实的样本级漏洞。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates two key weaknesses in the typical membership inference attack (MIA) evaluation pipeline, showing that aggregate vulnerability metrics reported in practice may not reliably reflect true sample-level vulnerabilities, as training sufficient shadow models is computationally infeasible.
